description: Recorded tool-call script for ECII Test E (generalization), a sensor bracket mounted to an existing industrial machine, replayed by the FAKE provider. It proves the same structure as Test A for an unrelated domain: intent, architectures, diversity and readiness through the real operations. It is not a model run and says nothing about reasoning quality. Domain words appear here as fixture values only.

turns.user: ^Design a bracket that mounts a vibration sensor to an existing industrial machine

arguments.rationale: The bracket holds a sensor on a machine that already exists, so it works with an existing system whose type and frame are not stated.

externalSystems.name: Industrial machine (type and frame not stated)
externalSystems.description: The machine the sensor is to be mounted on; its model and mounting surfaces are not given.

objectives: Hold a vibration sensor rigidly enough to measure the machine
environment: Industrial floor, vibration, possible oil and heat

questions.text: Which machine, and where on it should the sensor sit?
questions.why: The available mounting surfaces and the measurement point decide which attachment can work; guessing would risk a bracket that does not fit or measures the wrong thing.
options: Tell me the machine make and model
Upload photos or drawings of the machine
Supply measurements of the mounting surfaces

arguments.reason: ECII Test E: interpret the intent before designing

steps.final: I interpreted this as an accessory that mounts to an existing machine; the machine is not identified yet. Apply the intent to record it. I have not designed anything yet.

arguments.text: Ways to mount a vibration sensor on an existing industrial machine
arguments.name: Sensor mounting architectures

alternatives.name: Magnetic base on a flat surface
alternatives.summary: A magnet holds the sensor base to a flat steel surface.

architecture.hostInterface: A flat ferrous surface on the machine
architecture.interfaceGeometry: Surface size, flatness and coating are not known
advantages: No tools and no change to the machine
risks: Poor vibration coupling through a coating
architecture.attachmentPrinciple: Magnetic attraction between the base and the surface
architecture.loadPath: Sensor weight and vibration pass through the magnet face into the machine
architecture.installationRemoval: Place on the surface; pull off
disadvantages: Holding force falls with heat and coating
evidenceRequired: Surface material, finish and temperature at the measurement point

alternatives.name: Plate bolted to an existing tapped hole
alternatives.summary: A small plate is bolted to a tapped hole the machine already has.

architecture.hostInterface: An existing tapped hole near the measurement point
architecture.interfaceGeometry: Thread size, depth and position are not known
architecture.attachmentPrinciple: Plate clamped by a screw into the existing hole
architecture.loadPath: Vibration and weight pass through the screw and plate face into the machine
architecture.installationRemoval: Undo the screw, fit the plate, refasten
disadvantages: Needs a spare hole in the right place
evidenceRequired: Position, thread and depth of candidate holes

alternatives.name: Band clamp around a round housing
alternatives.summary: A strap clamp holds the sensor against a cylindrical part.

architecture.hostInterface: A cylindrical housing section near the measurement point
architecture.interfaceGeometry: Housing diameter and surface are not known
architecture.attachmentPrinciple: Strap tightened around the housing section
architecture.loadPath: Strap tension presses the sensor base against the housing
architecture.installationRemoval: Loosen the strap and slide the assembly off
disadvantages: Strap can creep or loosen under vibration

steps.final: I prepared three different ways to mount the sensor on the machine; each names the feature it depends on and the evidence needed, and none states a dimension I do not know. Apply to record them.

arguments.text: Magnetic base on a flat surface
